confidences.reason: The code’s state updates for when the second or third piston fires are incorrect. Per the rules, firing piston 2 or 3 should both eject the struck ball and also release (remove) the first-position ball; then the remaining ball(s) advance and two new ramp balls enter. In the simulation, after popping the struck ball at index 1 or 2, it does not remove the first-position ball; instead it inserts a ramp ball at the front (and another at index 1 for the third case), yielding wrong platform states. This misimplementation skews ejection frequencies.

The simulation logic in Step 1 misimplements the update rules when the second or third piston fires. It fails to remove the first-position ball (which should be released) and to move the third (or second) ball forward correctly, instead inserting new ramp balls improperly. Since this flawed core logic determines the computed probabilities, it is the first mistake leading to the wrong outcome.

Subsequent steps (Verification_Expert, Probability_Expert, and TheoreticalChemistry_Expert) accepted the simulation result of ball 2 without identifying or addressing any logical errors in the update rules, and the process was terminated. No correction was made after Step 1.
